strongest_bounded_proposition: Early Anglo-Saxon England is defensibly characterized as slaveholding in the broad period around 500 CE, though direct legal evidence begins later.
strongest_unsupported_proposition: Do not assign exact 500 CE prevalence or make Æthelberht's later law code contemporaneous.
territorial_practice_summary: Slaveholding is supported for early Anglo-Saxon society in broad-period synthesis.
legal_state_summary: Earliest English law code mentioning slaves dates 597–616.
temporal_scope_precision: Broad c.500 context supported; exact-date legal attestation is not.
inference_extent: No inference beyond stated target/evidence locus.
language_access_limitations: English-accessible packet only; non-English/non-digitized scholarship not exhaustively searched.
